---
title: "Reporting RMediation in a Paper"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(RMediation)
```

A result from RMediation is reproducible only if a reader knows which version produced it, which method and settings, and, for a stochastic method, the seed. This page lists what to record and report. It is a checklist, not a set of rules about what is statistically right.

## 1. Pin the version

CRAN serves RMediation 1.6.1. Later releases are on GitHub only, as pre-releases, and are not on CRAN. Report which you used, and install the exact tag so a reader can too:

```r
pak::pak("Data-Wise/rmediation@v1.9.0")
# or
remotes::install_github("Data-Wise/rmediation", ref = "v1.9.0")
```

Replace `v1.9.0` with the tag you ran. The [Releases page](https://github.com/Data-Wise/rmediation/releases) lists the tags. Do not cite `dev` or an untagged install: it moves.

Record what R reports for your session:

```{r version}
as.character(packageVersion("RMediation"))
```

`sessionInfo()` goes in a supplement or the project's `README`. A result that depends on OpenMx or medfit should also record those versions.

## 2. Report the method and its settings

| You used | Report |
|---|---|
| `medci()` | `type` (`"dop"`, `"MC"`, `"asymp"`), the confidence level, and `rho` if you set it |
| a Monte Carlo interval (`type = "MC"`, `ci()` with a formula) | `n.mc` and the seed |
| `ci()` on a `lavaan` fit | how each `:=` was handled: two coefficients honor `type`, exactly three get the exact interval, four or more and other formulas get Monte Carlo (see [Technical Notes](technical-notes.html), section 7) |
| `mbco()` or `mbco_product_null()` | `type`, `R` for a bootstrap, the seed, the OpenMx version, and any warning raised |

Name the interval as the package does: a distribution-of-the-product interval is not a "Sobel" interval.

## 3. Report the seed

A stochastic method (Monte Carlo, a bootstrap) is reproducible only with its seed. Set it immediately before the call and say so:

```{r seed}
set.seed(2026)
medci(mu.x = 0.5, mu.y = 0.6, se.x = 0.08, se.y = 0.04, type = "MC", n.mc = 1e5)
```

RMediation does **not** record the seed. It cannot be recovered from the random-number state afterward, so your analysis script has to say it. Run each stochastic call after its own `set.seed()` so a reader can reproduce it alone.

## 4. Use `@provenance` for `mbco()` results

From 1.10.0, an `mbco()` result records what produced it. Report these fields, or paste the printed block:

| Field | Holds |
|---|---|
| `rmediation`, `openmx`, `medfit`, `r` | package and R versions (`NULL` for a package not loaded) |
| `type` and `R` | the test type and the bootstrap size (`NULL` without a bootstrap) |
| `rng_kind` | `RNGkind()` at the time |
| `time` | when it ran |

Also report `@dropped` (bootstrap replicates that did not converge), `@refit` (when `h0` had to be refit) and `@branch` (for a product null). See [Testing an Indirect Effect with MBCO](mbco.html).

## 5. A methods sentence to adapt

> Confidence intervals for indirect effects were computed with the R package RMediation (version *x.y.z*, installed from the GitHub tag *vX.Y.Z*) using the *distribution of the product / Monte Carlo (n = *N*, seed = *S*)* method at the *95%* level. Likelihood-ratio tests used `mbco()` with *type* and, for the bootstrap, *R* = *R* replicates (seed = *S*), with OpenMx *version*.

Cite the method papers listed under [Citation](https://github.com/Data-Wise/rmediation#citation) in the README, and `citation("RMediation")` for the package itself.

## 6. Reporting a problem

When a result looks wrong, include the version, the call, the seed, `sessionInfo()` and, for `mbco()`, the printed provenance block in the [issue](https://github.com/Data-Wise/rmediation/issues). That is usually enough to reproduce it.
